correctness.rationale: For fixed r>=3, fixed pendant counts h_i>=0 and M_n/n->rho>0, each occupied vertex sends at TOTAL rate one to uniformly chosen neighbor. Detailed balance gives unique fixed-mass canonical weights product of degrees^{occupation}; hub degrees n+h_i, n peripheral vertices degree r and H pendants degree 1. The exact generating coefficient factors (1-(n+h_i)z)^(-1), (1-rz)^(-n), (1-z)^(-H). Sum over fixed outside s and pendant ell, compare with hub composition T_n(M): binomial(n+s-1,s)(r/n)^s -> r^s/s!, uniform exponential factorial upper bound dominates tails; pendant weights suppress positive ell. Conditional hub weak-composition Riemann sums and log(1+h_i/n) expansion yield the exponentially tilted simplex and independence from Poisson(r). Independently checked 468 exact detailed-balance transitions for K_{3,4} with one pendant and three particles, plus tilted-marginal mean at rho=1 equals (3-e)/(e-2)=0.392211..., rather than 1/3. These finite checks do not prove convergence.

value.rationale: A multi-hub network with asymptotically tied degrees and a finite degree perturbation is a natural symmetry-breaking condensation model. The theorem identifies a full r-1 dimensional tilted sharing law, an independent tight Poisson bulk and a macroscopic effect from just one pendant edge; these are substantive asymptotic observables beyond the classical stationary product measure or one-defect condensation story. It does not claim mixing-time or dynamic condensation results.

limitations: Unindexed work on nearly degenerate deterministic zero-range defects could give the same Dirichlet or tilted-simplex sharing law.
The finite canonical stationary formula is classical; originality is only the specific joint scaling law.
